oakA.notes: Broad, lumpy round crown with stepped edges. Not windswept or tiered. The short trunk and root flare sit on the ground. Lit from the upper left. Outline and shade steps match the house (v5_pv_oakA).

oakB.notes: Smaller, rounder crown on a slightly longer trunk. Distinct from oakA in size and proportion. No doubled rim (v5_pv_oakB).

bushC.notes: Now a low, wide, lumpy mound. Reads as a broadleaf garden shrub, no longer a cypress or cone (v5_pv_bushC_lime, v5_bushC_row_3x).

bushD.notes: Taller rounded mound with a stepped outline. Not a rectangle (v5_pv_bushD).

bushE.notes: Low, wide mound. No stem or lattice (v5_pv_bushE). Its silhouette is close to bushC; only the size and highlight differ.

canopy.notes: canopy_cmp after: reads as a mixed leafy mass. No tile seams. The bottom fringe is still a line of evenly spaced trunks on one y (canopy_after, y~135-140 at 1x), as it was before.

forest_crop.notes: RIGHT forest, bottom row (forest_crop_v5 x~660-760, y~460-525): three copies of the light oakA crown sit side by side at an exact 32px stride. Their tops and the dark undersides of the crowns line up on one horizontal line, and three trunks stand at equal spacing. The pixel match at the 32px shift is 83%; the BEFORE side at the same slots matches 44%. The result reads as an orchard row and a hedge wall, worse than before. The round-3 blocker is unresolved.

blocking_issues: forest_crop_v5.png RIGHT x~660-760 y~460-525: three pixel-identical oakA copies (83% match at a 32px stride vs 44% before) with aligned tops, a flat continuous crown underside and evenly spaced trunks. This is an orchard row. The new design's uniformity makes repeats in adjacent slots obvious. Vary the variant, flip or palette per slot, stagger trunk y, or let back crowns overlap the front trunks.
minor: bushC and bushE silhouettes are near-identical low mounds (v5_bushC_row_3x vs v5_pv_bushE).
Adjacent oak crowns in v5_row_test_3x form a repeated chevron or zigzag with a dark V crease between crowns. This is mechanical when they are packed.
Canopy bottom fringe is a line of evenly spaced trunks (pre-existing).
The dark ground-shadow block behind the forest has straight top and right edges (pre-existing, both sides).
